title: Kim Jae-yoon injury sidelines closer despite 35-save season - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Kim Jae-yoon injury sidelines closer despite 35-save season - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 25일(일) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Kim Jae-yoon injury sidelines closer despite 35-save season 
 입력 2026.10.25. 02:50 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Because it was an autumn stage he had waited for more desperately than anyone, the regret can only be greater.
 Samsung Lions closing pitcher Kim Jae-yoon was excluded from the playoff roster due to an unexpected injury. He helped the team finish second in the regular season by recording a personal single-season high of 35 saves this season, but he will not be able to join the important stage competing for a spot in the Korean Series.
 Kim Jae-yoon's wife also conveyed her sad feelings through social media. The whole family had been counting down to the playoffs, so the disappointment was great. In particular, she even expressed apologies to his teammates, which made viewers feel sorry.
 Kim Jae-yoon appeared in 64 games this season and recorded a 7-5 win-loss record, 35 saves and a 3.22 earned run average. He broke his personal single-season saves record and topped the league in this institutional sector, earning his first title since debut.
 Kim's role was significant in Samsung's direct advance to the playoffs. He took the mound in tight situations and preserved team victories, and based on his abundant experience he steadied the core of the relief corps. As a veteran he led by example and faithfully fulfilled the role of guiding younger players.
 But an unexpected injury came before the fall baseball season.
 While preparing to pitch in the second intrasquad game held at Daegu Samsung Lions Park on the 22nd, Kim Jae-yoon felt pain in his right levator scapulae. Detailed examination confirmed muscle and fascial damage.
 A team official explained, "There is bleeding along the fascia and the opinion is that it corresponds to a grade 1 injury. A rest of about two weeks is required."
 Manager Park Jin-man said, "Kim Jae-yoon had rested late in the season because his latissimus dorsi condition was not good, but this time the upper connecting area was damaged. Since he needs to rest for at least two weeks, postseason participation does not seem easy."
 Samsung, which must fill the closing pitcher's vacancy, plans to make changes to bullpen usage. Manager Park Jin-man said, "Rather than designating a specific player for save situations, we will put in the go-to relievers according to the flow of the game."
 Kim Jae-yoon's wife wrote on her Instagram, "We all waited for the playoffs more than anyone, so it's so disappointing, painful and I only feel sorry."
 She added, "Tears come from wanting to be together until the end, but because I know the uncles will do well even for dad's share, our family will cheer until the end at the ballpark."
 The family's disappointment is understandable. It must be more upsetting than anyone that Kim Jae-yoon himself cannot take the mound.
 But there is no reason to feel sorry. Samsung's ability to go directly to the playoffs as the second place in the regular season was greatly helped by Kim Jae-yoon's performance. He was responsible for the back door in moments when victory was desperate, and each of those results combined to create the current standing.
 Contributions that do not appear in the record cannot be overlooked. Combining outstanding skill and excellent character, Kim Jae-yoon, as a veteran, led the mood of the relief corps and became a solid support for younger pitchers. His role was clearly significant in the Samsung bullpen showing a strong performance this season.
 Of course, Kim Jae-yoon's absence is regrettable. In a short series a one-run game can determine the flow, and the presence of a reliable closing pitcher is that important. That said, Samsung's fall baseball should not be shaken by the injury of just one player, Kim Jae-yoon.
 Now it is the remaining players' turn to join forces. If the go-to relievers divide roles according to the situation as Manager Park Jin-man plans, and the batting order backs them with sufficient scoring, the bullpen's burden can be reduced. The best scenario is to win by a large enough margin that a save situation is unnecessary.
 In recent years Samsung has faced unexpected injury variables before the fall baseball season. Each time the remaining players joined forces to fill each other's vacancies. This time is no different.
 Even if Kim Jae-yoon cannot take the mound, he can still be a source of strength for his teammates. Based on his long experience, offering advice to younger players and encouraging them is also a veteran's role.
 The victories Kim Jae-yoon preserved throughout the regular season are now the ones his teammates must continue. If Samsung climbs higher on the autumn stage, that joy will be fully returned to Kim Jae-yoon and his family.
 Kim Jae-yoon's 35 saves were already a great help to Samsung this season. Just because he paused due to injury does not change that value.
